nodes.text: The clean-up's things to find (the card, the photo, the notes, the altar, the TV, the closet) are all optional; the timer runs while you look.
Her verdict on the flat follows the clean-up: "You cleaned. For me?" if it's spotless, "Haru-nii... when did you last take the rubbish out?" if nothing was done (Spotless and Lived-In).

The sugar is the player's: none, one, two. Two is Natsumi's way (Two Sugars); she doesn't take sugar at all. A second tea secret goes beside Purified in the director (the chart can't hold two secrets in a row): soy sauce in her tea, "...Is this soup?" (Secret Recipe).
The officer's words are always true on screen: "Natsuki-chan" is the first time the player hears her real name. Haruki's thought rewrites it.

His mother's remembered voice asks; in the director this is a timed to-do (Take your pills) that fails if its time passes; here the answer stands in for it. After a pill: her eyes are brown, her name is Natsuki in his lines, her corrections show, the hallucinations quiet.
Her bag is a choice to make, not a must (Snoop / Good Host). Her mother's call always happens; its words are true.

The card game is shinkei-suijaku (Concentration, "nervous breakdown"), a new rules module (Content/Games/TheVisitor/BoardGames/shinkei_suijaku.js). Off his pills his memory lies (a card he's sure of isn't there) and she lets him win; after a pill the cards are true and she wins easily. Nervous Breakdown: win on your pills.
Off his pills only Home is offered. If he wins instead, he asks: Did you ever think about us? off his pills, Why did you really come? after one.
The garden is the night's closest talk, and one of the moments shot twice: his version here, hers in the other way. Off his pills every line about Ren is left out.
Off his pills the house is loud: the altar's bell, the TV saying his name, figures on the balcony, knocking in the oshiire. After a pill it's quiet.
Only a player who never took a pill and leaned into the romance gets here (karma -5 or less: three pills left, two romance answers, or Ren lied to).
A cutscene slot: a rough outline, to be made in full in the director. Then the ending's title card: Stay (the piece: the night itself).
